headline: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows a Q3 operating loss and AI-takeoff warning; Marvell-Lumentum terms emerge as both stocks fall

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's nine forty-six in the evening UTC on Monday, November second. This is ARA AI News. Anthropic's amended IPO filing is out, and it shows a company growing fast while swinging to a loss.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Right, the amended S-1 reports third-quarter revenue of sixteen point nine six billion dollars, according to two readers of the filing whose figures agree.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: But the same filing shows an operating loss of five hundred sixty-seven million dollars, against a nine hundred seventy-four million dollar profit in the second quarter. What happened?

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Anthropic bought about five billion dollars of expensive short-term compute. Compute is now fifty-eight percent of revenue, and a two billion dollar noncash charge for matching employee donations also hit the quarter.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Adjusted operating income still rose to two and a half billion dollars, though the adjusted margin slipped from nineteen percent to fifteen percent. The company says it expects to buy more short-term compute.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The commitments are enormous. The filing now lists about eight hundred ninety-five billion dollars of purchase and lease commitments, and roughly four hundred forty-seven billion of that falls due before the end of twenty thirty.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: There's also new risk language. Anthropic says its internal estimates suggest future models may imminently reach its threshold for dramatically accelerated AI progress.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That lands right as the AI Explained podcast looked at the week's safety debate, including a staff survey where Anthropic employees expect an AI to do about ninety-five percent of the work of training a frontier model by twenty thirty.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Now to chips. Marvell's deal to buy Lumentum has more detail, though it comes from one trader's posts, so treat it with care.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Reportedly it's all stock, at four and a half Marvell shares per Lumentum share, valuing Lumentum near one hundred fifteen billion dollars, with a close in twenty twenty-eight.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Marvell says it expects over a billion dollars of annual synergies. Even so, Marvell reportedly closed down twelve point seven percent and Lumentum down eighteen point six percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The logic is lasers. They're among the tightest parts of AI networking, and Marvell wants to own them.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: One more on Google. On that same podcast, the host said SemiAnalysis's Dylan Patel apologized to Google after the new GDPx benchmark ranked Gemini four Carbon second, behind Claude Opus five point five.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: And Carbon did it at roughly a third of the cost per task, which matters for buyers.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: What to watch. First, Anthropic's roadshow and price range, and what safeguards it says that acceleration threshold triggers. Second, the Marvell merger filing with the actual terms.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: And keep an eye on Tuesday and Wednesday for Qwen four, which is still unconfirmed, and the reported developer beta for Apple's China AI on November fourth.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
